timeline.player_input: I shake the rain off my coat and step up to the desk. "I'm here about the Kestrel manifest."
"The seal drops at midnight tomorrow. After that nothing leaves this harbour."
"If anyone asks, you never saw me. Say the ledger was already signed."
"The number is four-seven-three-one. Write it somewhere you'll remember."
I glance at the door, then lower my voice. "How long have you worked here?"
"Who told you to wait for me tonight?"
I set a folded paper on the desk and slide it across without a word.
"That name on the paper. Have you seen it before?"
"Don't answer yet. Look at me properly first."
I pull off the wig and the coat. "I'm not who you were told to expect."
"Everything I said before tonight was someone else's script."
"My name is Wren. That much is true, and it's the only thing that is."
"The woman who was supposed to sit here tonight is in the harbour."
"I need the ledger. Not a copy. The one under your hand."
"Ask me anything and I'll answer it straight. You've earned that."
"The code I gave you earlier opens nothing. I made it up to see if you'd write it down."
"You wrote it down."
I take the pencil from her and cross the number out.
"There's a real number. I'll give it to you when I trust you."
"Someone is coming up the harbour road. Two of them."
I move to the lamp and turn it down to almost nothing.
"If they ask, I'm the auditor and you've never met me before."
"Whatever you hear in the next ten minutes, don't move."
"They're gone. You can breathe."
"You didn't give me up. I want to know why."
"The seal is real, by the way. That part was never a lie."
"Tomorrow at midnight this office stops existing. So do you, on paper."
"Come with me or don't, but decide now."
I hold out the ledger to her, open, and wait.
"Last chance. Say the number back to me."
